reason: When recovery codes are stored in user storage via CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:115-131), validation in UserCredentialManager.isValid (model/storage/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/UserCredentialManager.java:59-79) delegates directly to the UserStorageProvider's CredentialInputValidator.isValid and skips RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:99-116), while RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:70-92) never consumes the used code. Neither the SPI interfaces (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/CredentialInputValidator.java:27-37) nor the new helpers document that providers must consume used codes, as reflected by the patch's own BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid (testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:326-340) leaving codes reusable.
